auth.title: Authentication
highlights:
# Authentication

> Get access to the Waterfall API, send your API key in the x-api-key header, and manage keys for separate workflows.

Authenticate data and account API requests with your Waterfall API key in the `x-api-key` header. Contact the team for API access and pricing.

```http
x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY

```

> [!NOTE]
> 
> The API host is `https://api.waterfall.io`. Data endpoints use `/v1/`; Account Reporter V2 uses `/v2/account`. Use the path shown on each reference page.

## Best practices

- Store keys in server-side environment variables. Keep them out of browser code and public repositories.
- Rotate keys periodically.
- Use dedicated sub-keys to manage access and usage for separate teams or workflows. Creating and managing sub-keys requires a master API key.

Missing keys return `401`. Invalid keys return `403`; this status can also indicate that a feature or permission is unavailable to the key. Inspect the error `code` using the Errors guide.

Follow the quickstart to make your first request, or use Agent Skills to build with an agent.

This documentation is built and hosted on Mintlify, a developer documentation platform.

# API Keys - Create

> Create a sub-key to track and manage API usage for a team, environment, or integration.

Create a sub-key under your Waterfall account. Each key has a label, active status, and request rate limit. See API key management for how sub-keys fit into your integration.

> [!NOTE]
> 
> Requires your master API key in the `x-api-key` header.

## Label the integration

`notes` is required. Use a label that identifies where the key will be used.

```json
{
  "notes": "signup-enrichment",
  "per_interval": 30
}

```

If omitted, `per_interval` defaults to `50` requests per 60 seconds. It cannot exceed the master key's `per_interval`. Set it explicitly when the master key's limit is lower or you want a smaller limit for this integration.

auth.title: Errors
highlights:
# Errors

> Resolve Waterfall API validation, authentication, quota, rate-limit, and job errors using HTTP status and machine-readable error codes.

Read the HTTP status and the response's `code` to decide what to do next. For a successful job request, also read the job's `status` before using the output.

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `200` | Request succeeded. An asynchronous launcher has accepted a job; its data may still be processing. |
| `400` | Invalid inputs. Correct the fields identified by the error before retrying. |
| `401` | Missing API key. Add the `x-api-key` header. |
| `402` | Account over quota. Check usage and account access before sending more requests. |
| `403` | Invalid key, insufficient permission, or a feature not enabled for this key. Read `code`. |
| `404` | Requested resource or job was not found. Check the identifier and endpoint. |
| `429` | Rate limit exceeded. Follow `Retry-After`. |
| `500` | Internal server error. Keep the response and any known job ID for troubleshooting. |

gate.title: Waterfall API FAQ
highlights:
### What is Waterfall used for?

Waterfall.io is a B2B data API for go-to-market workflows.

Use Waterfall to find people at target accounts, enrich contact and company records, match emails to business profiles, find phone numbers, verify email addresses, and check job changes.

...

### What does Waterfall's multi-vendor approach mean?

Waterfall combines 30+ data vendors through one API. Coverage varies by provider, so a contact or field missing from one source may be available from another. We evaluate providers on coverage, accuracy, freshness, and cost, and add or remove them as their performance changes.

Your team maintains one integration and one set of agreed Waterfall rates, without managing separate vendor connections and contracts. Changes to the vendor mix do not change those rates. Your total cost depends on the services and options you use and your request volume.

...

## Access, usage, and pricing

### How do I get an API key and pricing?

API access is available by approval. Enter your work email on the Waterfall website to request a key, or book a call to discuss your workflow and pricing. A member of our team reviews every access request; we aim to reply within a couple of hours. We work with a limited number of customers so we can provide direct support and plan capacity around each team's needs.

Once you have a key, send it in the `x-api-key` header. Follow Authentication and the Quickstart.

### Does my API key enable every capability?

Waterfall API access depends on the features enabled for your key. A valid key can receive a permission error for an unavailable capability, and adding `include_phones: true` requires phone enrichment access. Confirm the capabilities your workflow needs with the Waterfall team, and use the Errors guide to interpret the returned code.

### How do I see what a request cost?

When `output.usage` is present in a Waterfall result, it reports `total_usd`, counts and costs by category, and `balance_remaining_usd`. For an asynchronous job, retrieve the result before reading its cost. Usage Tracking explains the fields. Count each job once when totaling costs; prices in example responses are illustrative, not a price list.

### Am I charged when nothing is found?

Waterfall billing rules differ by endpoint. Phone Enrichment charges only when a number is returned. Email Verification does not charge for results where `output.email.email_status` is `unknown`. For other operations, follow the endpoint's billing guidance, your agreed rates, and the result's usage breakdown. Contact our team to confirm how missing or partial results are charged in your planned workflow.

### Can I track usage separately for teams or workflows?

Yes. Use a Waterfall master key to create labeled sub-keys for different integrations. Authenticate Account Reporter with a sub-key to compare its `key_usage` with overall `account_usage`. Product prices are returned only to master-key requests. See API key management for creating keys and managing their request limits.

### Can I set a spending cap for an agent?

Set the agent's authorized budget in your execution workflow. Waterfall's `output.usage` helps you track reported job costs, but a balance snapshot does not reserve money for requests already in flight. A sub-key's `per_interval` limits request rate, not dollars spent. See Usage Tracking before designing spending controls for parallel calls.

### Can I process a list of records?

Yes. Your integration can process a list through individual Waterfall requests within your account's rate limits. Contact Enrichment, Company Enrichment, Phone Enrichment, and Email Verification accept one subject per request. Search endpoints have their own result limits or pagination. See CRM enrichment for connecting results to a list of records.

### Can Waterfall support higher request volumes?

Yes. The default for Prospector, Search, Enrichment, Job Change, and Email Verification is 50 requests per 60 seconds. It is not Waterfall's maximum capacity: we can support volumes more than 10 times higher with the right account and workflow configuration. Email support@waterfall.io with your APIs and expected volume so we can agree on limits for your setup. Your integration must follow the limits configured for its key.

### Which endpoints are in Preview?

Search Company and Company Titles are marked Preview in these guides. Their behavior may change; discuss your requirements with our team before using them in a critical workflow. See their endpoint references for supported inputs and results.

## Building an integration

### Can Waterfall help build a custom data pipeline?

Yes. We can help you choose APIs, benchmark the fields your product needs, and build a custom data pipeline. Bring your starting inputs, required outputs, expected volume, and destination, such as a CRM, Snowflake, or a Clay table. Customers work directly with our founders in a dedicated channel to plan the integration and review results.

...

A synchronous Contact Enrichment option is also available by arrangement for enterprise customers. Contact our team for access details.

...

### Can I use Waterfall with ChatGPT, Codex, Claude, Grok Bot, or Cursor?

Yes. ChatGPT, Codex, Claude, Claude Code, Grok Bot by xAI, and Cursor can use Waterfall's API documentation to help plan and build integrations. Follow Build an integration to create reusable code. To run live lookups, the agent needs HTTP-capable code or tool execution and an authorized Waterfall API key.

### What does an agent need to run a Waterfall lookup?

To run a lookup, the agent needs an environment that can make HTTP requests and an authorized Waterfall API key. Give it the published OpenAPI file, the relevant endpoint reference, and your task, starting inputs, required fields, and criteria for a useful result. Choose an API helps you select the reference.

Store the authorized API key in the agent's execution environment rather than in its prompt. Define the records, actions, and budget allowed for live calls, which follow your account's usage and billing terms. Have the agent retrieve the completed output and check it against your criteria before claiming a match. Skills provide optional request and integration guidance; installing them does not provide API access.

gate.title: Pricing | How Waterfall.io pricing works
highlights:
# Pay for answers, not for lookups

Outcome-based across every endpoint: a credit is deducted when we return a verified result, never once per vendor we queried to find it

## Three rules that decide what you pay

A miss costs nothing

Billing

We are charged by our vendors on every request we make on your behalf, including the ones that come back empty. You are not. A credit is deducted only when we hand back a verified result, so the risk of a low-coverage file sits with us rather than with your budget.

One credit covers the whole waterfall

Coverage

A single request may pass through several of our 30+ sources before one returns a verified answer. You are charged once, for the answer. This is the structural difference from buying vendors directly, where each contract you add multiplies your cost per record whether or not that vendor was the one that found it.

Rates are quoted against your data

Commercials

Per-credit rates depend on the endpoints you use and the volume you commit to. We quote after running a benchmark on a sample of your own records, because a list price set against someone else's file tells you nothing about what your file will cost.

Why there is no public rate card

Straight answer

Because a per-record price is not comparable across vendors and we would rather not pretend otherwise. Two providers quoting the same cent-per-email can differ by a factor of three on what fraction of your file they actually resolve, and the cheaper one is usually the more expensive one once you divide by results. The number that matters is your cost per verified result on your records, and the only honest way to produce it is to run both against the same file. We will do that before quoting, and we will show you the working.

...

## What moves your cost per result

The identifier you send

A professional email or a LinkedIn URL resolves more often, and in fewer hops, than a name plus a company domain. Better inputs mean fewer paid-for misses upstream and a lower blended cost.

Which endpoints you call

Mobile numbers cost more than emails because the underlying data costs more. Job-change checks are cheap to run at scale because unchanged contacts are never billed.

How hard your records are

Enterprise contacts in North America resolve on the first source. Smaller companies, non-standard email patterns and coverage outside a vendor's home region go deeper into the waterfall — the same price to you, a different cost to us.

What you commit to

Per-credit rates fall with committed volume and term. Platforms reselling enrichment downstream are priced differently from teams enriching their own CRM, because the volume shape and the support load are different.

## FAQ

How does Waterfall.io pricing work?

Outcome-based, on credits. A credit is deducted only when we return a verified result — a verified email, a matched profile, a mobile number, a confirmed job change. Requests that come back empty are free, and one credit covers the entire waterfall regardless of how many of our 30+ sources we had to query to get the answer. Per-credit rates depend on the endpoints you use and the volume you commit to, and are quoted after a benchmark on a sample of your own records rather than from a list price.

Is it cheaper than buying the vendors directly?

It depends on how many vendors you need, and the honest answer is that one vendor is usually cheaper on paper. The arithmetic changes as you add the second and third: buying direct means paying each contract in full whether or not it was the one that resolved a given record, plus the minimums, the separate integrations and the schema-mapping work. With a waterfall you pay once per result. The crossover is usually around the second vendor, and it arrives sooner the harder your records are.

What counts as a billable result?

A result we return to you that meets the verification bar for that endpoint. For email, that means a verified address rather than a pattern guess. For phone, a mobile number rather than a switchboard line. For job change, an actual detected move — a contact who has not moved is never billed, which is what makes running your whole CRM on a weekly schedule affordable. Every response carries a usage object so you can reconcile what you were charged against what you received, per request.

Is there a free trial, and is there a minimum?

Before anything is signed we run a benchmark on your data at no cost: send a sample of records your current vendors missed and we return coverage and cost per result against what you are paying today. Commitments and minimums are set at contract and depend on volume and term — if you would rather not commit before seeing numbers on your own file, the benchmark is designed for exactly that.

## Book a call to hear more

Every company has different needs. Talk to our team (most likely one of the founders) to share your use case and see how Waterfall can help.

mcp.title: Run a Waterfall lookup with an agent
highlights:
# Run a Waterfall lookup with an agent

> Use the waterfall-direct-api skill to retrieve contact or company data and verify emails through Waterfall HTTP API calls.

Use `waterfall-direct-api` when you want an agent to retrieve data for a task now: a contact lookup, a company lookup, a verification check, or a small evaluation. The skill guides HTTP requests, authentication, result handling, pagination, and errors.

For a maintained workflow in your application, use Build an integration.

## Install the skill

```bash
npx skills add Waterfall-io/api-skills --skill waterfall-direct-api

```

The skill is published in the Waterfall API Skills repository. API calls require an authorized Waterfall key; installing the skill does not provide access. Store the key in the execution environment, as described in Authentication.

## Example task

> I have three LinkedIn profile URLs. Use Waterfall to return each person's available name, job title, and company name, with the original URL beside each result. Choose the endpoint from the current docs. I do not need emails or phone numbers. Show the requests before making live calls, and leave unavailable fields empty.

This task gives the agent a known input, specific output fields, and a record limit. Choose an API explains which endpoint fits. See use cases for other starting points.

## Review the result

Check that the result answers your task and that missing matches or fields remain visible. A completed API job does not guarantee a complete profile. Use the returned job ID to retrieve asynchronous results rather than launching the lookup again.

Read Usage Tracking for costs when they are available in the result. Calls use your account's configured rates.

Use the current endpoint reference if it differs from the skill's instructions. For code that your team will maintain, continue to Build an integration.

# One GTM API for contacts and companies

> Find prospects, enrich contact and company profiles, find emails and mobile numbers, verify emails, and check job changes with the Waterfall API.

Waterfall brings together 30+ data vendors through one B2B data API. Find people at target accounts, match emails to business profiles, find contact details, and check whether existing contacts have changed jobs.

Use it to build signup enrichment, prospecting, and CRM workflows with the data your team needs. About Waterfall explains how it fits into your stack.

> [card] Explore use cases
> 
> Start with a signup, target account, or CRM record and see the workflow.

> [card] Use with agents
> 
> Run a lookup with an agent or build Waterfall into your application.

> [card] Evaluate Waterfall
> 
> Compare useful results, match quality, and cost on your own records.

> [card] Make your first request
> 
> Launch a contact enrichment job and retrieve its result.

Already know what you want to build? Choose an API to compare the inputs, results, and availability of each capability.

## What do you want to build?

| Your task | Start here |
| --- | --- |
| See who is behind a signup email | Signup enrichment |
| Find people at your target accounts | Account prospecting |
| Fill gaps in contact and company records | CRM enrichment |
| Check where existing contacts work | Job changes |
| Check an email before outreach | Email verification |
| Identify companies visiting your website | Website company identification |

## How the API works

Send requests to `https://api.waterfall.io` with your API key in the `x-api-key` header. Authentication covers access and key management.

Prospector and the contact, phone, and company enrichment APIs return a `job_id`. Use the matching Finder to retrieve the result, or provide a `webhook_url` to receive it. Search and verification APIs return results in the same request. The API selection guide lists the response pattern and availability for each capability.

Every reference page shows the supported inputs and outputs. Use Usage Tracking to read returned costs, and Account Reporting for usage across a date range.

For API access, pricing, or help choosing the right workflow, talk to the Waterfall team. Common product and integration questions are covered in the FAQ.

# Build a Waterfall integration with an agent

> Use the waterfall-integration skill to create Waterfall API integration code in your own Python, JavaScript, or TypeScript project.

Use `waterfall-integration` when Waterfall will be part of your application or a recurring workflow. The skill guides an agent to create Python or JavaScript/TypeScript integration code in your repository, using your stack and conventions. Your team owns and maintains that code.

For a lookup you want to run now, use Run a lookup.

## Install the skill

```bash
npx skills add Waterfall-io/api-skills --skill waterfall-integration

```

The skill is published in the Waterfall API Skills repository. It provides integration guidance. Live API calls still need an authorized key and follow your account's usage and billing terms.

## Describe what you want to build

Give the agent your starting inputs, required output fields, and the place where the workflow belongs in your application. Specify your existing HTTP client, how results should be stored, and whether the task includes live calls.

The skill includes a live API call to verify the generated code. If you only want code and mocked tests, say so explicitly, as in the example below.

For example:

> Add Waterfall Contact Enrichment to our signup workflow. Start with the signup email and use our existing HTTP client. Save the returned job ID with the signup record and retrieve the result. Map available title and company fields into the enrichment record; keep missing fields empty and do not overwrite existing CRM values. Leave phone enrichment off and keep the API key on the server. Add mocked checks for running, completed, and failed jobs. Do not make live API calls in this task.

Start with signup enrichment for the workflow and Quickstart for the request sequence. Use Choose an API for other tasks.

## What to review in the integration

Confirm that the code uses the documented inputs, reads the result fields your task needs, and handles missing data and unsuccessful jobs. Your integration decides when to submit requests and how to update your own records.

See Authentication, Errors, and Usage Tracking for API behavior. The current endpoint references take precedence if the skill's instructions differ.

This documentation is built and hosted on Mintlify, a developer documentation platform.
